subject: Learning Methods
title: Hitting Easy Too Often
description: A 60-second lesson on Hitting Easy Too Often.

hook.text: She rated every card 'easy' to speed through reviews. A month later, half her mature cards had been forgotten.

buildup.text: Rating cards easy inflates their intervals beyond what your memory can support. The schedule becomes unrealistic.

discovery.text: Honest self-assessment is critical. The algorithm only works when your ratings reflect true recall difficulty.

twist.text: A card you struggled with but answered correctly should be rated 'good,' not 'easy.' Struggle matters for scheduling.

climax.text: Reserve 'easy' for cards that feel effortless. Use 'good' as your default. Accuracy is more important than speed.

punchline.text: Rate honestly. The algorithm trusts your judgment.

quiz.question: What happens when you consistently rate cards as 'easy'?
options: The cards are permanently removed from the deck
Intervals inflate beyond what your memory can support
